summary: GCP Service Perimeter (VPC-SC) blocking Workload Identity cross-project assume-role for oncall observability tasks
description: Issue summary: Oncall engineers are unable to use the standard ops Workload Identity -> cross-project assume-role flow to access observability resources (log sinks / monitoring dashboards) in prod. Impact: multiple runbook operations relying on short-lived WIF-based impersonation fail, causing extended page response times and manual escalation.
impact: Oncall and SRE unable to perform standard incident triage steps (read logs, tail pods, query traces) for production clusters in us-central1. Pager escalations increased, some SOPs blocked for >3 hours.
environment_details: Prod projects: proj-prod-core (services), proj-prod-observability (log sinks, dashboards). Shared VPC hosted in proj-net. Workload Identity Pools mapped in proj-ops; the ops WIF principal should be able to assume iam roles in proj-prod-observability via iam.workloadIdentityUser -> serviceAccount impersonation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a GKE pod in proj-prod-core, invoke gcloud auth login using workload identity token for ops-sa@proj-ops. 2) Attempt to impersonate sa-observe@proj-prod-observability with --impersonate-service-account. 3) Observe DENIED errors referencing 'Access denied by service perimeter' in audit logs.
logs_observed: Error sample from audit: 'request denied by VPC Service Controls: Access to proj-prod-observability/logging.sinks.list was blocked by service perimeter: perimeter-prod'. Stacktrace: gcloud returns HTTP 403 with errorDetails VPC_SC_PERIMETER_VIOLATION. Cloud Audit log link: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query; sample entry id: 12345abcde
investigation_notes: - Initial hypothesis: recent perimeter update tightened allowed access types for projects outside the perimeter. - Reviewed perimeter configuration (perimeter-prod) and found an ingress rule change 2026-03-09 that removed 'accessLevels' exceptions for proj-ops. - Workload Identity tokens are issued from proj-ops WIF and therefore classified as 'request from outside perimeter' by VPC-SC. - Compared to INT-489205 (WIF mapping/autoscaler reports) and INT-214159 (impersonation during private deploy), pattern differs: here the perimeter denies service account impersonation rather than WIF pool mapping errors. - Tested temporary workaround: add proj-ops to perimeter's 'resources' list or create an explicit ingress rule for iam.googleapis.com and logging.googleapis.com; both approaches allowed impersonation in dev replica when applied.
temporary_workaround: Applied a scoped ingress rule to perimeter-prod allowing iam.googleapis.com and logging.googleapis.com calls from proj-ops for a 1-hour window to restore oncall access. Notified Security and applied strict audit around the window. Workaround reverted after stabilization and a safer policy planned.
root_cause: Change to perimeter-prod on 2026-03-09 inadvertently removed a narrowly-scoped service ingress exception used by ops WIF. The tightened perimeter treats cross-project WIF-based impersonation as external traffic and blocks iam:serviceAccounts.get/impersonate calls when originating from proj-ops.
resolution: Coordination with Security and Cloud Platform teams to add a targeted ingress rule that allows iam.googleapis.com (service account impersonation) and logging.googleapis.com for the specific workload identity pool principals (ops WIF) rather than adding entire project resources to the perimeter. Patch rolled out 2026-03-11 at 23:10 UTC with staged verification.
postmortem_actions: - (Action) Create CI check that validates VPC-SC perimeter diffs for removing service ingress exceptions dependent on ops WIF (owner: Security, due 2026-03-20). - (Action) Update Oncall runbook to include VPC-SC contact points and temporary ingress rule playbook (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-17). - (Action) Add an automated integration test that simulates WIF->impersonation from ops pools against prod observability APIs (owner: Infra QA, due 2026-03-24).
follow_up: Security to review broader perimeter rules to ensure no other short-lived tokens are impacted. Consider moving critical observability service accounts into the same perimeter or use VPC-SC access levels for bounded exceptions.
